videos.title: Waiting for the Stock Market Crash? See What Happened the Last 24 Times
videos.description:
Is a stock market crash coming? Wars, rate hikes and oil shocks have all hit before, and in 23 of the last 24 midterm cycles (96%), going back nearly 100 years, the S&P 500 still finished higher from late September to July.

On Monday, September 28, 2026, the S&P 500 enters a seasonal window that has finished higher in 23 of the last 24 midterm election cycles, going back to 1930. The median gain was +18.9%. In this video I put today's headlines next to 95 years of data, one fear at a time, and show what happened every time this window opened under scary news:

• 1990 Gulf War: oil doubled, then fell 44% in the window. The S&P 500 rose 28%.
• 2022, the fastest rate hikes in 40 years: +24.9%
• 1994, the Fed doubled rates: +20.9%
• 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis: +22.8%
• 1966 Six-Day War: +19.7%
• 2002 Iraq: +20.1%
• 1942 World War II: +41.2%
• 1974 oil shock: +43.5%
• 1998 bubble fears: +34.2%

And the honest part: 2018 fell 19.5% inside the window before finishing +2.8%, 1930 was the one loss (-23.4%), and a drop of more than 20% from Monday's close would be deeper than any winner on record. That is the line I'm watching for Observation Twenty-Five.

videos.title: 2026: The Market Level Hidden in 100 Years of Data
videos.description:
Worried about a 2026 stock market crash? If you own stocks or S&P500 ETFs, this video shows how much downside a strong historical record can hide and the level no previous winning cycle crossed.

Across 24 completed midterm windows in The 100-Year Pattern, the S&P500 finished higher 23 times. Yet the 2018 window fell 19.5% below its starting price before finishing higher. The only losing window began in 1930. A strong win rate does not show you how painful the journey can be.

Using real TradeWave charts, I compare the 2018 recovery with the 1930-31 failure. You will see how to measure the roughly 20% reference below the September 28, 2026 starting close, and why falling past it would exceed the deepest decline in any previous winner in this record. I also explain why a deep loss at the end of the window would make me question whether the market itself has changed.

CHAPTERS
0:00 The 100-Year Pattern: 23 of 24 finished higher
0:20 Why 2026 looks dangerous
0:58 The -20% line I am watching
1:20 What TradeWave shows us
1:36 The exact 2026-2027 window
2:08 How I found the pattern
3:06 MFE and MAE: what the green bars hide
3:45 The 2018 recovery and the 1930 failure
4:19 Three possible outcomes
4:50 What crossing the -20% line would mean
5:45 Trump, the midterms and the market
6:17 How I will track Observation 25

THE DATES AND THE LEVEL
The pattern runs from September 27 of a U.S. midterm-election year through July 18 of the following year. That is 295 calendar days, counted inclusively. This is a midterm-year study, not an every-year pattern.

For 2026-2027, both endpoints fall on Sunday, so TradeWave uses the next trading closes: September 28, 2026, and July 19, 2027.

The roughly -20% reference is measured from that September starting close, not today's price or an all-time high. Crossing it would exceed every previous winner's downside in this record. It would not by itself prove another Great Depression or rule out a recovery.
